rationale: Both candidates independently surface the same underlying fact the ground truth's sole inline concern (trust_remote_code/kernels-version fragility) was already resolved by a later commit, and both flag the same secondary issues (stale PR body, uncovered test, possibly-unrelated red NPU CI check), so recall is essentially tied and full. X's strongest original catch is a genuine, diff-native correctness bug (a module missing required symbols gets cached before validation, so a bad load is 'sticky' and skips retries) and ships two ready-to-merge suggestion diffs, giving it a slight actionability edge. Y's findings are marginally more precise and cohesive: it demonstrates actual verification (stubbed kernels module, checked against installed kernels 0.16.0) and its dead-code/version-pin-mismatch finding directly deepens the exact 'kernels version compatibility' theme the human reviewer raised, whereas X's coverage of that theme mostly just reports it as already fixed. Neither has a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
